taxonomyNote: NatureServe's standard name is 'Pine Woods Littersnake'; 'Pine Woods Snake' is given as an alternate name.
fieldMarks: Slender, smooth-scaled snake, usually 25-33 cm (to about 40 cm); yellowish-brown to reddish-brown, paler on the lower sides.
Dark line from the snout through the eye to the jaw corner; lips plain white or yellowish in Florida but often dark-speckled in the north and west of the range.
Belly white, cream or yellowish; 17 scale rows behind the neck, divided anal plate, round pupils.
Often a faint dark stripe down the middle of the back and another on each side.
behavior: Secretive and fossorial; found under loose bark, in or under rotting logs and stumps, leaf litter or buried in sandy soil.
Active on the surface chiefly at night; most active in spring and may be active year-round.
Eats small amphibians and reptiles (lizards, frogs, salamanders); rear teeth deliver a mild venom to immobilise prey and it does not bite when handled.
Lays 2-4 eggs, usually in rotting wood, from late April or May through August.
habitat: Damp pine flatwoods, slash and longleaf pine woodland maintained by periodic fire; also hardwood hammocks near flatwoods, sandhills near water and wooded wet-prairie edges.
range: Southeastern coastal plain of the United States only: Alabama, Florida (most of the peninsula south to near Lake Okeechobee plus the central panhandle), Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, North Carolina and South Carolina.
